document.description: HscA (Hsc66) is a specialized cytosolic Hsp70-family chaperone encoded with its J-type co-chaperone HscB in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It has a low intrinsic ATPase activity, limited by ATP hydrolysis rather than nucleotide exchange, and needs no GrpE-type exchange factor. Its substrate-binding domain recognizes a conserved LPPVK loop of the Fe-S scaffold protein IscU, and HscB delivers IscU to the ATP-bound state of HscA; together IscU and HscB stimulate HscA ATP hydrolysis about 500-fold, trapping IscU in the ADP-bound complex. ATP hydrolysis by the 1:1:1 HscA-HscB-IscU[2Fe-2S] complex distorts the IscU-bound cluster and accelerates [2Fe-2S] cluster transfer to acceptor apoproteins such as ferredoxin, so HscA acts as the ATP-driven engine of cluster release in Isc-mediated Fe-S protein maturation. HscA also binds cluster-deficient biotin synthase and improves its in vivo [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly, and its expression is induced by cold shock. Direct conformational measurements show preferential stabilization of disordered IscU, consistent with a holdase-like mechanism; a general folding or refolding role is not established by these cluster-transfer experiments.

review.summary: HscA, with HscB and ATP, catalyzes the transfer of [2Fe-2S] clusters from holo-IscU to acceptor apoproteins and improves in vivo cluster assembly on biotin synthase.
review.reason: HscA does part of the work of the process: its ATP hydrolysis drives the structural change in the IscU-bound cluster that accelerates transfer, and an ATPase-dead HscA cannot accelerate transfer. This is the core biological process of HscA. GO:0016226 is kept at this level (rather than [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly) because the Isc pathway that HscA serves matures acceptors carrying several cluster types.

document.description: HscB (Hsc20) is a 171-residue cytosolic J-type co-chaperone encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It has an N-terminal J domain that contacts the dedicated Hsp70 HscA (Hsc66) and a three-helix C-terminal domain whose conserved hydrophobic and acidic patch binds the Fe-S scaffold protein IscU. HscB stabilizes the structured conformation of IscU and delivers IscU (apo or cluster-bound) to HscA, lowers the IscU concentration needed to activate HscA, and synergistically stimulates HscA ATP hydrolysis several hundred-fold. The resulting HscA-IscU-HscB ternary complex drives the ATP cycle that releases and transfers IscU-assembled Fe-S clusters to acceptor apoproteins, so HscB acts as the targeting and ATPase-activating component of the Isc Fe-S cluster biogenesis machinery. A weak interaction with the cysteine desulfurase IscS has also been reported.

review.summary: HscB stimulates the ATPase activity of its dedicated Hsp70 partner HscA, modestly alone and synergistically (hundreds-fold) together with IscU.
review.reason: The InterPro HscB family mapping is borne out directly by E. coli biochemistry: purified HscB (Hsc20) stimulates HscA (Hsc66) ATPase activity and, with IscU, raises it more than 400-fold, while HscB itself has no ATPase activity. This is the core molecular activity of HscB.

supported_by.supporting_text: Addition of both Hsc20 and IscU to Hsc66 resulted in a dramatic stimulation, increasing the ATPase activity of Hsc66 ≈100-fold over the level observed in the presence of Hsc20 or IscU alone and >400-fold over the basal intrinsic activity.
purified IscU and Hsc20 alone did not exhibit detectable ATPase activity
Previous studies have shown that IscU and HscB individually enhance HscA ATPase activity modestly (≅4−8-fold) but together can synergistically stimulate activity up to ≅400-fold

review.summary: SPR and ITC show that HscB binds the Fe-S scaffold IscU directly (1:1, Kd about 13 uM); the interaction is real and functionally central.
review.reason: Per the protein-binding policy, bare GO:0005515 is removed as uninformative; removal does not dispute the HscB-IscU interaction. Its functional content (HscB targets IscU to HscA and activates HscA ATPase) is captured by GO:0001671 ATPase activator activity and by HscB membership in GO:1990230 iron-sulfur cluster transfer complex, both kept in this review. GO has no specific MF term for binding the IscU scaffold.

supported_by.supporting_text: Surface plasmon resonance and isothermal titration calorimetry further showed that IscU and Hsc20 form a complex, and Hsc20 may thereby aid in the targeting of IscU to Hsc66.

review.summary: Ni-affinity co-purification and yeast two-hybrid detected HscB associating with HscA and with IscU.
review.reason: Bare protein binding is uninformative. description: HscB (Hsc20) is a 171-residue cytosolic J-type co-chaperone encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx
  operon. It has an N-terminal J domain that contacts the dedicated Hsp70 HscA (Hsc66) and a three-helix

  ATPase-activating component of the Isc Fe-S cluster biogenesis machinery. A weak interaction with the
  cysteine desulfurase IscS has also been reported.

document.description: IscS is the housekeeping pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent cysteine desulfurase of Escherichia coli, a cytosolic homodimer encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It converts L-cysteine to L-alanine and carries the released sulfane sulfur as a persulfide on its active-site Cys328, located on a flexible surface loop. From this persulfide IscS delivers sulfur to a range of acceptor proteins that bind one at a time around Cys328: the scaffold IscU for assembly of [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] clusters (with frataxin/CyaY, IscX and ferredoxin acting as modulators of the IscS-IscU complex); ThiI for 4-thiouridine formation in tRNA and for thiazole/thiamine biosynthesis; TusA, the entry point of the Tus relay that leads to MnmA-catalysed 2-thiolation of the wobble uridine; and FdhD for maturation of molybdenum formate dehydrogenases. IscS also degrades L-selenocysteine in vitro and has been implicated in selenium delivery for selenophosphate synthesis. Loss of IscS abolishes tRNA s4U and causes thiamine and nicotinic acid auxotrophy and slow growth.

description: 'IscS is the housekeeping pyridoxal 5''-phosphate (PLP)-dependent cysteine desulfurase of
  Escherichia coli, a cytosolic homodimer encoded in the iscRSUA-hscBA-fdx operon. It converts L-cysteine
  to L-alanine and carries the released sulfane sulfur as a persulfide on its active-site Cys328, located
  on a flexible surface loop. From this persulfide IscS delivers sulfur to a range of acceptor proteins
  that bind one at a time around Cys328: the scaffold IscU for assembly of [2Fe-2S] and [4Fe-4S] clusters
  (with frataxin/CyaY, IscX and ferredoxin acting as modulators of the IscS-IscU complex); ThiI for 4-thiouridine
  formation in tRNA and for thiazole/thiamine biosynthesis; TusA, the entry point of the Tus relay that
  leads to MnmA-catalysed 2-thiolation of the wobble uridine; and FdhD for maturation of molybdenum formate
  dehydrogenases. IscS also degrades L-selenocysteine in vitro and has been implicated in selenium delivery
  for selenophosphate synthesis. Loss of IscS abolishes tRNA s4U and causes thiamine and nicotinic acid
  auxotrophy and slow growth.'

document.description: HscA (PP_0846) is the specialized Hsp70-family ATPase of the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 Isc system. Its ATPase cycle is stimulated by HscB and is coupled to IscU-dependent iron-sulfur cluster transfer. The conserved mechanism involves nucleotide-dependent scaffold binding and release; homolog studies distinguish this specialized cycle from generic refolding of damaged proteins.

review.summary: ATP binding is integral to the scaffold-transfer cycle.
review.reason: ATP binding is required for the HscA nucleotide cycle and is distinct from hydrolysis. It is a core mechanistic property, not peripheral merely because a catalytic term is more informative. Target curated HscA activity supports the conserved binding claim.

supported_by.supporting_text: Has a low intrinsic ATPase activity which is markedly stimulated by HscB.

review.summary: IscU transfer activity does not alone establish or exclude protein folding.
review.reason: The term concerns assistance in formation of correct tertiary structure, not breadth of client range. E. coli HscA preferentially binds disordered IscU and slows its transition to the structured state in PMID22782893. ATP-dependent cluster transfer is well supported, but a target folding endpoint is unresolved. Do not infer generic folding solely from Hsp70 membership or reject all folding solely from specialization.

supported_by.supporting_text: Has a low intrinsic ATPase activity which is markedly stimulated by HscB.

review.summary: HscA supplies ATP-dependent assistance to the cluster-transfer stage.
review.reason: Curated target maturation function and HscA-specific signatures support this role. Homolog ATPase-defective mutant experiments show dependence of cluster transfer on the nucleotide cycle; they are not KT2440 mutant assays.

supported_by.supporting_text: Chaperone involved in the maturation of iron-sulfur cluster-containing proteins.
A mutant form of HscA lacking ATPase activity, HscA(T212V), was unable to accelerate cluster transfer

review.summary: ATP hydrolysis is the supported catalytic activity.
review.reason: Hydrolysis drives the specialized scaffold-transfer cycle. The target HAMAP activity and the homolog ATPase-defective mutant support a core ATPase assignment; no generic foldase activity is needed to make the catalytic claim.

PMID22782893 finds stabilization of disordered IscU, not a target folding endpoint. This is insufficient precision for an active NEW assertion, not proof that HscA can never assist any folding reaction. ## Function
- Specialized Hsp70 (Hsc66). ATP hydrolysis is rate-limiting [PMID:10713091 "These results indicate that ATP hydrolysis is the rate-limiting step under steady-state conditions and is >10(3)-fold slower than the rate of ADP/ATP exchange."]
- IscU is its substrate, recognized through the LPPVK motif [PMID:12871959 "Hsc66 interacts with peptides corresponding to a discrete region of IscU including residues 99-103 (LPPVK)"]; [PMID:15485839 "IscU behaves as a substrate for HscA, and HscB enhances the binding of IscU to HscA."]
- Catalyzes ATP-dependent cluster transfer [PMID:18986169 "HscA-mediated acceleration of [2Fe2S] cluster transfer exhibited an absolute requirement for both HscB and ATP."]
- Binds BioB and improves its in vivo cluster assembly [PMID:19821612 "In this work, we show that in Escherichia coli, HscA significantly improves the efficiency of the in vivo assembly of the [2Fe-2S](2+) cluster on BioB under conditions of low to moderate iron."]
- Cold-induced [PMID:7665466 "Expression of hscA was not induced upon heat shock but was induced approximately 11-fold 3 h after a shift from 37 to 10 degrees C."]

PMID:22194618, PMID:24561554 and PMID:18304323.

## Biochemical activity

- IscS is a PLP-dependent cysteine desulfurase: it converts L-cysteine to L-alanine
  and a protein-bound persulfide. [PMID:8663056 "This E. coli protein contains pyridoxal phosphate as a cofactor and catalyzes the removal of sulfur from cysteine to form alanine and S0."]
- Persulfide on Cys328. [PMID:11972033 "Cys-328 of IscS attacks the sulfur atom of L-cysteine, and the sulfane sulfur derived from L-cysteine binds to the Sgamma atom of Cys-328."]
- C328A abolishes cysteine desulfurization but much less so selenocysteine
  decomposition. [PMID:10739946 "The enzyme activity toward L-cysteine was almost completely abolished by the mutations, whereas the activity toward L-selenocysteine was much less affected."]
- In vitro IscS also degrades L-selenocysteine to alanine. [PMID:10739946 "All three homologs catalyze the elimination of Se and S from L-selenocysteine and L-cysteine, respectively, to form L-alanine."]
  UniProt records a physiological selenium-delivery role for selenophosphate synthesis.
- Crystal structure, PLP on Lys206; Cys328 on a mobile loop. [PMID:12860127 "Cys328 is positioned greater than 17A from the pyridoxal phosphate cofactor"]
- Homodimer; each subunit binds one IscU (UniProt SUBUNIT, PMID:11577100, PMID:12860127, PMID:22203963).

## Sulfur-donor hub

- Master sulfur donor. [PMID:20404999 "The cysteine desulfurase IscS is a highly conserved master enzyme initiating sulfur transfer via persulfide to a range of acceptor proteins involved in Fe-S cluster assembly, tRNA modifications, and sulfur-containing cofactor biosynthesis."]
- Acceptors bind one at a time near Cys328. [PMID:20404999 "The sulfur acceptors can only bind to IscS one at a time, while frataxin and IscX can form a ternary complex with IscU and IscS."]
- Fe-S assembly: sulfur transfer to IscU via a Cys328–Cys63 disulfide-linked complex
  [PMID:11972033 "We here report that a covalent bond is formed between Cys-328 of IscS and Cys-63 of IscU."];
  IscS can donate sulfur to build the [4Fe-4S] cluster of dihydroxy-acid dehydratase
  [PMID:8663056]; isc operon coexpression boosts holo-ferredoxin yield [PMID:10393315].
- CyaY (frataxin) binds IscS and gates cluster formation [PMID:19305405 "CyaY participates in iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly as an iron-dependent inhibitor of cluster formation, through binding to the desulfurase IscS."].
- tRNA s4U8: IscS -> ThiI -> tRNA [PMID:10753862 "the sulfane sulfur generated by IscS is transferred sequentially to ThiI and then to tRNA during the in vitro synthesis of s(4)U."]; deletion abolishes s4U [PMID:10781607 "In frame deletion of the iscS gene in Escherichia coli results in a mutant strain that lacks s(4)U in its tRNA."].
- tRNA mnm5s2U34: IscS -> TusA -> TusBCD -> TusE -> MnmA [PMID:16387657 "IscS transfers the persulfide sulfur to TusA."].
- Thiamine (thiazole) and NAD: [PMID:10781607 "the iscS(-) strain requires thiamin and nicotinic acid for growth in minimal media"]; IscS mobilizes sulfur to ThiS thiocarboxylate.
- Molybdenum enzymes: IscS -> FdhD -> formate dehydrogenase [PMID:22194618 "The interaction of IscS with FdhD results in a sulfur transfer between IscS and FdhD in the form of persulfides."].
- RhdA (A. vinelandii rhodanese, heterologous) is persulfurated by IscS [PMID:16310786].

## Curation judgements (summary)

- Core: cysteine desulfurase activity (GO:0031071) + sulfur carrier activity
  (GO:0097163) driving Fe-S cluster assembly (GO:0016226/GO:0044571); second core
  branch: sulfur donation to tRNA thiolation (GO:0002143, GO:0002937).
- Non-core: thiamine biosynthesis, selenocysteine lyase/catabolism, L-cysteine
  catabolism (chemically correct but describes sulfur mobilization), transient
  shared [2Fe-2S] ligation with IscU.
- Removed: detection of UV (NAS; s4U-tRNA, not IscS, is the near-UV chromophore);
  bare protein-binding rows from interactome screens. Sulfur compound transport
  marked over-annotated: persulfide relay between proteins is not transport.


## 2026-11-07 ISC whole-gene re-review

Retained the independent thiamine and tRNA sulfur-delivery branches as core work. Sulfur-compound transport includes intracellular directed transfer and is supported by persulfide handoff, not restricted to a pore. The electronic [2Fe-2S] binding claim is unresolved: the structural intermediate highlighted in PMID36605734 derives from Archaeoglobus IscS–IscU(D35A), while native E. coli ligand occupancy is not established. No claim that transient binding cannot be a molecular function.

All original ordered annotation payloads and historical NEW actions were preserved. Existing raw/provider/publication files were not refreshed. # hscA curation notes

- Q88PK4 is the dedicated HscA-family ATP-dependent chaperone encoded in the KT2440 isc locus.
- ATP hydrolysis is mechanistically correct but under-specific. The core molecular function is ATP-dependent protein folding chaperone activity because HscA uses its ATPase cycle with HscB to remodel cluster-bearing IscU.

## Isc comparative-evidence audit (2026-11-07)

HscA (PP_0846) is the specialized Hsp70-family ATPase of the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 Isc system. Its ATPase cycle is stimulated by HscB and is coupled to IscU-dependent iron-sulfur cluster transfer. The conserved mechanism involves nucleotide-dependent scaffold binding and release; homolog studies distinguish this specialized cycle from generic refolding of damaged proteins.

The target remains KT2440; no purified target assay is claimed. Specific curated HAMAP/RuleBase statements or independent NCBIfam/InterPro signatures ground the target inference. ARBA names are not used as proof. All original ordered source payloads are retained. The rows are IEA or historical NEW, not IBA; no donor-count argument, PAINT loss or new evolutionary node placement is asserted.

A genuine Falcon request failed with HTTP 403 authentication/access failure. Existing OpenScientist reports, where present, were preserved; no provider-branded replacement was fabricated. The log is `.cache/module-audit-logs/isc-20261107/psepk-consultation/falcon-hscA.log`.

### Evidence and biological limits

- [PMID:18986169] ATPase-defective HscA fails to stimulate cluster transfer in the characterized homolog system. Quoted support: “A mutant form of HscA lacking ATPase activity, HscA(T212V), was unable to accelerate cluster transfer”.
- [PMID:22782893] E. coli HscA stabilizes disordered IscU and acts as a holdase in the studied conformational cycle. Quoted support: “HscA decreases the D → S rate and binds to and stabilizes the disordered state of IscU”.

### Decisions

- GO:0005524 ATP binding: ACCEPT. ATP binding is required for the HscA nucleotide cycle and is distinct from hydrolysis. It is a core mechanistic property, not peripheral merely because a catalytic term is more informative. Target curated HscA activity supports the conserved binding claim.
- GO:0006457 protein folding: UNDECIDED. The term concerns assistance in formation of correct tertiary structure, not breadth of client range. E. coli HscA preferentially binds disordered IscU and slows its transition to the structured state in PMID22782893. ATP-dependent cluster transfer is well supported, but a target folding endpoint is unresolved. Do not infer generic folding solely from Hsp70 membership or reject all folding solely from specialization.
- GO:0016226 iron-sulfur cluster assembly: ACCEPT. Curated target maturation function and HscA-specific signatures support this role. Homolog ATPase-defective mutant experiments show dependence of cluster transfer on the nucleotide cycle; they are not KT2440 mutant assays.
- GO:0016887 ATP hydrolysis activity: ACCEPT. Hydrolysis drives the specialized scaffold-transfer cycle. The target HAMAP activity and the homolog ATPase-defective mutant support a core ATPase assignment; no generic foldase activity is needed to make the catalytic claim.
- GO:0140662 ATP-dependent protein folding chaperone: NEW (retired historical proposal). Withdraw this inherited proposal from active use: GO0140662 requires ATP-driven assistance to protein folding, whereas the reviewed evidence establishes specialized IscU-state selection and cluster transfer. PMID22782893 finds stabilization of disordered IscU, not a target folding endpoint. This is insufficient precision for an active NEW assertion, not proof that HscA can never assist any folding reaction. The original ISS/file payload and row order are preserved; existing GO0016887 supplies the supported catalytic core.

The existing NEW GO:0140662 proposal is explicitly retired, not deleted or relabeled. ATP hydrolysis GO:0016887 was already present and is now the core catalytic term. The specific IscU-transfer mechanism remains in biological descriptions; absence of a proven target folding endpoint is not universal evidence against all protein-folding activity.

- Q88PK5 is the HscB-family co-chaperone encoded in the KT2440 isc locus. UniProt/HAMAP supports its dedicated Isc-system role.

## Isc comparative-evidence audit (2026-11-07)

HscB (PP_0845) is the J-domain cochaperone of the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 Isc system. It binds the Hsp70-family partner HscA and stimulates ATP hydrolysis. Its conserved specialized family supports recognition of the IscU scaffold and coupling to cluster transfer, with the detailed interaction and conformational cycle established in bacterial homologs.

The target remains KT2440; no purified target assay is claimed. Specific curated HAMAP/RuleBase statements or independent NCBIfam/InterPro signatures ground the target inference. ARBA names are not used as proof. All original ordered source payloads are retained. The rows are IEA or historical NEW, not IBA; no donor-count argument, PAINT loss or new evolutionary node placement is asserted.

A genuine Falcon request failed with HTTP 403 authentication/access failure. Existing OpenScientist reports, where present, were preserved; no provider-branded replacement was fabricated. The log is `.cache/module-audit-logs/isc-20261107/psepk-consultation/falcon-hscB.log`.

### Evidence and biological limits

- [PMID:18986169] ATP-dependent HscA/HscB cluster-transfer reconstitution supports the cochaperone role and transient complex participation. Quoted support: “HscA-mediated acceleration of [2Fe2S] cluster transfer exhibited an absolute requirement for both HscB and ATP.”.
- [PMID:22782893] E. coli HscB preferentially binds structured IscU whereas HscA stabilizes its disordered form.

### Decisions

- GO:0001671 ATPase activator activity: ACCEPT. The target HAMAP SUBUNIT statement directly assigns stimulation of HscA ATPase; homolog biochemical studies explain this conserved role. HscB is the activator, not an independently assigned ATPase.
- GO:0006457 protein folding: UNDECIDED. Client specificity alone is not grounds to reject protein folding. E. coli HscB stabilizes structured IscU and participates in an ATP-dependent cluster-transfer cycle, but that endpoint is not itself a test of assisting formation of the correct tertiary structure in KT2440. Retain uncertainty rather than claiming that specialization excludes folding or that a generic J-domain proves it.
- GO:0044571 [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly: ACCEPT. Curated target HscB function and ATPase stimulation, together with homolog cluster-transfer reconstitution, support involvement in this assembly process. This does not assign sulfur mobilization, cluster synthesis catalysis or direct cluster binding to HscB.
- GO:0051087 protein-folding chaperone binding: MODIFY. Use the supported Hsp70 partner identity to specify the binding claim. This replacement describes the known target partner and does not infer that HscA is a general refolding enzyme. The dedicated interaction is independently curated by HAMAP; its detailed target affinity has not been measured.
- GO:0051259 protein complex oligomerization: UNDECIDED. GO0051259 includes oligomers of different subunits. HscB participation in an IscU-HscA transfer complex is compatible with that definition, and isolated monomeric HscB would not refute it. However, complex membership and an oligomerization-domain name do not by themselves demonstrate that KT2440 HscB promotes oligomer creation. Without a resolved target assembly mechanism, retain uncertainty rather than REMOVE.
- GO:1990230 iron-sulfur cluster transfer complex: ACCEPT. Specific HscB identity, curated HscA binding and activation, and homolog ternary-complex reconstitution support transfer-complex membership. The published stoichiometry is experimental context for homologs, not a measured native KT2440 stoichiometry.
